whyWrong: B. A WAF protects a specific published web application. It is a real preventative control, but it is scoped to internet-facing web apps rather than to landing zones generally, which is what the stem describes.
C. Defender for Cloud alerts are detective, not preventative: an alert fires after suspicious activity is already observed, which is the opposite of preventing it.
E. Sentinel is a SIEM outside the secure score's control set entirely. Enabling it changes nothing in the score.

source.title: Just-in-time machine access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

std/208.explanation: The three requirements map onto one pairing. Just-in-time VM access keeps RDP and SSH closed by default in the network security group and opens them only for an approved request, for a limited window, which is what "only provide permission to connect… when required" means and what removes the need to leave 3389 and 22 open to the internet at all. Azure Bastion is the piece that makes the connection happen "by using the Azure portal": it is a browser-based, TLS-tunnelled RDP/SSH client built into the portal, with no public IP needed on the target VM and no client software to install.
whyWrong: A. PIM as VM Contributor grants standing role eligibility. It manages who may act, not when a network port is open or how the connection is made.
B. A VPN Gateway gives broad network-level reachability into the virtual network, the opposite of a narrowly scoped, portal-based connection, and does nothing to gate when 3389/22 are reachable.
C. Just Enough Administration scopes PowerShell remoting to specific cmdlets for specific roles. It has no bearing on RDP/SSH port exposure or portal-based connections.

source.title: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management overview

std/222.explanation: Both requirements need the devices under Microsoft's endpoint stack before anything else can happen, and threat and vulnerability management is what keeps them hardened afterward. Onboarding the kiosks to Intune and Defender for Endpoint is the prerequisite step: Intune is what lets you apply an application control policy restricting the kiosks to only authorized executables, and Defender for Endpoint onboarding is what turns on the endpoint security stack, including TVM, in the first place. TVM then continuously surfaces new misconfigurations and missing updates across the fleet, which is the "regularly harden against new threats" half of the requirement, ongoing rather than one-time.
whyWrong: A. Azure Monitor collects telemetry and metrics. It neither restricts what runs on a device nor recommends hardening changes.

B. A Privileged Access Workstation is a hardened admin endpoint for people performing sensitive administrative tasks. A public self-service kiosk running as a fixed, locked-down front-end is a different problem, restricting untrusted end users, not protecting a privileged operator.
C. Automated investigation and response triages and remediates alerts after a threat is detected. It does not restrict which applications may run or surface hardening recommendations.

source.title: Azure AD B2C smart account lockout

std/237.explanation: Identity-based attacks against a B2C sign-up/sign-in flow are password spraying, credential stuffing and brute-force guessing, and B2C's built-in smart account lockout is the control aimed squarely at that: it tracks failed attempts per account and per IP and blocks further tries once a threshold is crossed, all without any code in the application. Conditional Access integration with B2C user flows and custom policies adds the second, complementary layer, letting the application team require MFA or block risky sign-ins as part of the same authentication journey rather than bolting a check on afterward.
whyWrong: B. Workbooks visualise risk detections after the fact. They detect and report; they don't prevent an identity attack from succeeding.

C. Custom ROPC flows in B2C are a documented anti-pattern here: ROPC collects the raw username and password directly in the app and bypasses the interactive sign-in experience, which also bypasses MFA and Conditional Access. Recommending it works against securing the app, not for it.
D. Access packages in Identity Governance manage workforce entitlement requests and reviews. B2C is a consumer-identity product; there is no workforce entitlement lifecycle to govern here.

source.title: Configure active monitoring for OT networks

std/245.explanation: "Minimize the risk of disrupting business operations" is close to a direct quotation of Microsoft's own warning about the alternative: "active monitoring runs detection activity directly in your network and may cause some downtime," which is precisely why Defender for IoT defaults to agentless, passive monitoring for legacy OT equipment that can crash or misbehave under direct probing. Passive traffic monitoring gets visibility without ever touching the fragile devices, and threat monitoring is the analysis layer built on that same non-intrusive traffic capture, together delivering security awareness with none of the operational risk active scanning carries.
whyWrong: B. Active scanning is the technique Microsoft explicitly cautions against for exactly the disruption reason in the stem: "take care when configuring active monitoring so that you only scan necessary resources," precisely because it can cause downtime on the devices it touches.
D. Software patching is a remediation activity, not a monitoring methodology, and for legacy OT equipment it is frequently the change most likely to cause an outage, not the one that avoids it.

source.title: Use compliance policies to set rules for devices you manage with Intune

std/252.explanation: Blocking a specific OS build from reaching Microsoft 365 needs two things working together: a rule that defines what counts as compliant, and a gate that enforces it at access time. An Intune device compliance policy is where you set the minimum allowed Windows 11 build number, and a device that reports an earlier build is marked noncompliant. A Conditional Access policy then requires device compliance for access to Microsoft 365 services, so a device Intune has already flagged as noncompliant is blocked at sign-in. Neither policy alone does the job: compliance evaluation with nothing reading its result changes nothing, and Conditional Access with no compliance signal to check has nothing to gate on.
whyWrong: A. A Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance policy assesses Azure resource configuration against a standard. It has no visibility into client Windows build numbers.
B. A Defender for Endpoint endpoint security policy configures antivirus and attack-surface-reduction settings on devices; it does not report OS build compliance to Conditional Access.
C. A sign-in risk policy reacts to anomalous authentication behaviour, not to which Windows build a device is running.

source.title: Azure Blueprints retirement

std/18.explanation: Flagged because the second half of the keyed pair does not fit the requirement, and no other option is clearly the intended second answer either. Assigning an initiative to a management group is well supported: initiatives bundle many policy definitions under one assignment, so adding or removing an ISO 27001 control from the monitored set means editing the initiative once rather than touching 50 separate subscription-level assignments, which is exactly what minimizing modification effort calls for. The keyed second answer, assigning a blueprint to a management group, does not belong alongside it: a blueprint is a packaged deployment artifact combining templates, RBAC and policy assignments, not a live monitoring construct you edit to adjust which controls are being watched, and Azure Blueprints itself is being retired, with a phased retirement beginning in 2026 and full retirement on 31 January 2027. None of the remaining four options, per-subscription policy or initiative assignments, a per-subscription policy at the management group, or a per-subscription blueprint, better completes a two-part answer either, since each either multiplies the maintenance work across 50 subscriptions or repeats the same flaw as the keyed second option. The key is left as the source has it and the item is flagged rather than guessed at.

source.title: Just-in-time machine access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

std/99.explanation: The three keyed actions replace a single choke-point RDP server with a Zero Trust access path built for a remote, latency-sensitive contractor team. Migrating from the Remote Desktop server to Azure Virtual Desktop removes the shared jump-box and its custom administrative tools, giving each developer a session that terminates close to the Azure resources instead of hairpinning through Seattle. Azure Firewall restricting host pool outbound access (host pool is the AVD term for the set of session hosts) hardens that new AVD deployment's egress rather than leaving it wide open. Conditional Access with MFA and named locations then applies explicit, per-sign-in verification for a workforce connecting from France, which is the identity control a Zero Trust design substitutes for trusting the network path.
whyWrong: A. Restricting NSGs to specific IP ranges is a network-perimeter control from the model Zero Trust is replacing, and static IP allowlisting for developers in France does nothing to reduce the latency of relaying through a single Seattle-based server.

E. Deploying a second Remote Desktop server into a French Azure region still centralises access through a jump-box with locally installed admin tools, which is the pattern the redesign is meant to retire, not relocate.
